question:
Find the median from the following data.

 
 

 Age in years
 15-25
 25-35
 35-45
 45-55
 <td st
solution:
**Given:**

Age in years (Class intervals) = [15-25, 25-35, 35-45, 45-55, 55-65, 65-75, 75-85]

Number of patients (Frequency) = [11, 18, 22, 30, 40, 16, 33]

**Formula used:**

Median = L + dfrac{((N)/(2) - CF)}{f} × h

Where:

 
• L = Lower boundary of the median class
 
• N = Total frequency
 
• CF = Cumulative frequency before the median class
 
• f = Frequency of the median class
 
• h = Class width

**Calculations:**

Total frequency (N) = 11 + 18 + 22 + 30 + 40 + 16 + 33

⇒ N = 170

Median class: Class interval containing dfrac{N}{2} = 85

Cumulative frequency:

[11, 11+18=29, 29+22=51, 51+30=81, 81+40=121, 121+16=137, 137+33=170]

Class interval containing 85: 55-65

Values for formula:

L = 55, CF = 81, f = 40, h = 10

Median = 55 + dfrac{(85 - 81)}{40} × 10

⇒ Median = 55 + dfrac{4}{40} × 10

⇒ Median = 55 + 1

⇒ Median = 56

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**
